Context (f.36): F(α,β,γ) = 2F1(α,β;γ;x) = Σ_r (α)_r(β)_r/(r!(γ)_r) x^r, and F' = dF/dx. Gauss derives the contiguous relations, always expressing the shifted F and F' in the basis {F(α,β,γ), F'(α,β,γ)}. His method is to compare the coefficient of x^r in each function with C = the coefficient of x^r in F(α,β,γ). This is the tableau on f.38.

[4] Shift α→α+1 of F'. Previous page: relative to C, the coefficient of x^r in (1-x)F'(α+1,β,γ) is (α+r)(αβ+β+(α+β-γ+1)r)/(α(γ+r)). Hence the combination (α+1-γ)F'(α,β,γ) - α(1-x)F'(α+1,β,γ) has coefficient -β(α+r)C. That is the coefficient of -αβ F(α+1,β,γ) - βx F'(α,β,γ), using [2]. Solving gives
 F'(α+1,β,γ) = β/(1-x)·F + (α-γ+1+βx)/(α(1-x))·F'.
(My independent check: differentiate [2], F(α+1) = F + (x/α)F', and eliminate F'' with Gauss's ODE x(1-x)F'' = αβF - (γ-(α+β+1)x)F'.)

[5] The same with α↔β (symmetry of F in α,β):
 F'(α,β+1,γ) = α/(1-x)·F + (β-γ+1+αx)/(β(1-x))·F'.

[6],[8] Write [2] and [4] with α→α-1. Unknowns are G = F(α-1,β,γ) and H = F'(α-1,β,γ):
 F = G + xH/(α-1),
 (1-x)F' = βG + (α-γ+βx)H/(α-1).
Subtracting β times the first equation from the second gives (1-x)F' - βF = (α-γ)H/(α-1), so
 [8] H = -(α-1)β/(α-γ)·F + (α-1)(1-x)/(α-γ)·F'.
Then G = F - xH/(α-1):
 [6] F(α-1,β,γ) = (α-γ+βx)/(α-γ)·F - (x-xx)/(α-γ)·F'.
[7],[9] are the β-analogues.

Conclusion stated on the page: from F and F' one can rationally obtain F(α+k,β+l,γ) and F'(α+k,β+l,γ) for all integers k,l.

[10] The coefficient of x^r in F(α,β,γ-1) is C(γ-1+r)/(γ-1) = C(1 + r/(γ-1)). Hence
 F(α,β,γ-1) = F + x/(γ-1)·F'.

[11] The coefficients of x^r in xF'(α,β,γ-1) and F'(α,β,γ-1) are C·r(γ-1+r)/(γ-1) and C(α+r)(β+r)/(γ-1). So the coefficient in (1-x)F'(α,β,γ-1) is C(αβ+(α+β+1-γ)r)/(γ-1). This corresponds to (αβF + (α+β+1-γ)xF')/(γ-1), giving
 F'(α,β,γ-1) = αβ/((γ-1)(1-x))·F + (α+β+1-γ)x/((γ-1)(1-x))·F'.

[12],[13] Put γ→γ+1 in [10] and [11]. Unknowns are G = F(α,β,γ+1) and H = F'(α,β,γ+1):
 F = G + xH/γ,
 (1-x)F' = (αβ/γ)G + (α+β-γ)xH/γ.
Eliminate H using αβ - γ(α+β-γ) = (α-γ)(β-γ):
 [12] G = -(α+β-γ)γ/((α-γ)(β-γ))·F + γ(1-x)/((α-γ)(β-γ))·F'.
Then H = γ(F-G)/x. Using (α-γ)(β-γ) + γ(α+β-γ) = αβ:
 [13] H = αβγ/((α-γ)(β-γ)x)·F - γ²(1-x)/((α-γ)(β-γ)x)·F'.

Purpose: this is the systematic derivation of the contiguous relations of the Gauss hypergeometric series. It leads (f.38) to the theorem that any F, F' with parameters shifted by integers is a rational combination of F and F'. The page is a draft of the material in Gauss's 'Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam' (1812/13).
errors: [5]: the last function is written F'(α,β,x); it should be F'(α,β,γ). This is a pure notational slip.

[6] and [7]: before (x-xx) there is a smudged or erased factor, apparently (α-1), resp. (β-1). The correct coefficient of F' is just -(x-xx)/(α-γ), resp. -(x-xx)/(β-γ), with no such factor. The erasure suggests Gauss caught this himself (the factor belongs in [8],[9]). If the factor is read as standing, the formula is wrong.
[13]: the sign before the second term appears overwritten (+ corrected to −). The final − is correct.
All other formulas [4], [8]–[12] check out exactly. The coefficient-comparison justifications are correct but terse (the elimination steps for [4], [6]–[9], [12], [13] are left implicit).

results.what: Contiguous relations expressing F(α±1,β,γ), F(α,β±1,γ), F(α,β,γ±1) and their x-derivatives linearly over Q(α,β,γ,x) in the basis F(α,β,γ), F'(α,β,γ)
results.modern_name: Gauss contiguous relations for 2F1 (in derivative form)
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam (1812, publ. 1813)

results.what: Any F, F' with parameters shifted by integers is a rational combination of F and F' (the module of contiguous functions has rank 2)
Method of proof by comparing ratios of coefficients of x^r (tableau of coefficients)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the contiguous relations Gauss published in 1812/13. The F/F' formulation and the coefficient tableau are recognisably his published approach, so the page adds only draft-level detail (slips and corrections).
